result.title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
result.summary: Code generation models are increasingly used to produce interactive artifacts, such as websites and user interfaces. Many properties that determine whether these interfaces are useful only become apparent through realistic interaction, making them difficult to incorporate into model training. In this paper, we introduce RELIEF (REvision-based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback), a method for improving code generation models using feedback on their generated interfaces. RELIEF uses a coding agent to revise these interfaces, then incorporates the improvements into their original generation traces to produce supervision for fine-tuning. To evaluate RELIEF, we collected a dataset of 200 synthetically generated websites paired with 355 interaction recordings and accompanying feedback from 24 users. We used critiques derived from code inspection, automated interaction, explicit human feedback, and human interaction recordings to fine-tune variants of two code generation models. Our results show that feedback effectiveness varies with base model capabilities, with critiques inferred from human interaction recordings leading to the largest usability improvements overall under our tested models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RELIEF：用 coding agent 依据代码检查、自动交互与真实用户反馈修正模型生成的交互界面，再把修正结果回填进原始生成轨迹以构造微调监督，并在 200 个合成网站与 355 段用户交互记录上比较不同反馈来源的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把修正后的结果回写为原始生成轨迹监督」的做法，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索，但其任务与多模态推理无直接联系。
